newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales thin $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales thin $63 - feedlots.

text.p: CHICAGO, June 6 Reuter) - U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales Friday were very slow following active trade this week that set a record weekly large movement in Kansas, feedlot sources said.

Sales Friday consisted of 400 heifers at $63.00 per cwt that will likely grade select and choice in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said. The light sales were in contrast to the weekly movement of 131,700 head.
There were no reported sales in Kansas following the record weekly movement of 146,500 head, which surpassed the previous record by 10,100 the week ended August 22, 1996.
Sales at $63.00 were down $1.00 from the bulk of cattle that sold on Tuesday, down $2.00 from last Friday's brisk trade and off $3.00 from last week's top.
"This has not been a good week for the cattle owner," one Panhandle feedlot manager said.
Fed cattle prices were pressured by large supplies of market-ready cattle, feedlot sources said. Prices could be weakened next week by more of the same, feedlot sources said.
Pressure could be limited by this week's strong beef movement and reports that most feedlots were current, which could give cattle owners leverage, they said.
